description: The bytes a device puts on the wire for `POST /sync/push`, and which module contract each one routes to. Hand-authored as a *device* sends them — omitting every property the mutation does not use — because that is the exact shape both sides got wrong: the client sent every payload under `visit`, and the server made `visit` a required constructor argument. Neither suite could see it, because the client mocked the API and the server serialised a fully-constructed record, which always writes `"visit": null`. See ../README.md.

mutations.name: a visit worked offline
mutations.why: The original mutation type, and the only one until W9 slice 9. Kept first so a change to the shared envelope shows up here before it shows up in the three that came later.

mutations.name: a call the rep could not make
mutations.why: The case that shipped broken twice. The payload travels under `notVisited`, and `visit` is absent entirely — not null. A server whose `Visit` parameter has no default rejects this whole batch with a 400 before any routing runs, and a 400 is retried on every reconnect forever rather than recorded and stopped.

mutations.name: a call moved to another day
mutations.why: `date` is a plain `yyyy-mm-dd` with no time and no zone, because a planned call is dated to a business day rather than to an instant (BR-PRD-6). A client sending an ISO timestamp here would bind on some servers and shift the call by a day near midnight on others.

mutations.name: a call nobody planned
mutations.why: A shop and a day and no call id, because this one does not exist yet — and no plan id either, because a pulled round is flat calls with no plan on them. Journey resolves which round covers the day.

mutations.name: what a rep measured at a shelf
mutations.why: The audit is its own mutation (W10 slice 0), queued in the visit's own transaction: `/sync/push` answers per mutation precisely so one refusal cannot take a completed visit with it. `weightSetVersion` is the field the whole of `BR-AUD-8` rests on — the server resolves *that* published weighting and scores against it, never the current one. Note what the payload omits: no score, because the device's number is for the rep's screen and the server's is the record, and no outlet, because that comes from the visit.

mutations.name: an audit that is only a questionnaire and a photograph
mutations.why: A shop that would not let the rep count the shelf still lets them answer questions and take a picture, and that is a real audit (W10 slice 3b). Every optional slot the other case fills is omitted here rather than sent as null — which is the property this file exists to pin, and the one a serialised record would have silently broken.

mutations.name: a kind this server does not carry
mutations.why:
Bound, then refused by name at the routing arm rather than at the parser. The distinction matters to a device: `sync.push.typeUnsupported` is a per-mutation result it records and stops retrying, where a parse failure fails the entire batch. There is no `outbox` half — no client produces this, and the case exists to pin what happens when a newer device meets an older server.

This case named `CapturedAudit` until W10 slice 6, when the server learned to carry it. That the file had to change is the point: a vector pinning "unsupported" is a claim with a shelf life, and `CapturedOrder` is the next one to expire (W11).
